title: Deboli and Gołuchowski, St Petersburg 1786-1787 (AGAD Zbiór Popielów 3): 14 despatches in the older Polish code read in part with the key of the time ZbPop 444 (partial reading explained)

steps.what: Key of the time ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska' (8 Mar 1783) found and transcribed in full (1,965 entries); identified as the older code of 1783-88, not the 1789-91 code.
Key tested on three 1788 despatches with the cabinet's clears (ciphers hashed first): 0.874, 0.874, held-out 0.837; criterion >= 0.90 fixed in advance: failed; controls 0.08-0.12.
ZbPop 3 sorted by opening group (444 = 22 pieces; 9933, 3865, 12282, 4000); 14 pieces in code 444 transcribed.
14 pieces read by sense, blind to the clears: 7040 words, 5499 certain, 256 probable, 4 restored, 1281 unresolved (81.8%); blind shape plates Z3a and Z3G applied.

outcome.method_basis: Read with the key of the time ZbPop 444, transcribed from its scans; the key was tested on 1788 pairs and failed our 0.90 threshold (0.837), so every piece is offered as a partial reading explained.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored words excluded), counted by script on reading/*.md: 7040 words, 5499 certain, 256 probable, 4 restored, 1281 unresolved = 5755/7036 = 81.8%; per piece 0.696-0.905.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered test of the key of the time on three 1788 despatches with the cabinet's clears (ciphers hashed before the clears): read by sense 0.874, 0.874 and 0.837 on the held-out pair (0.864 overall), against shuffled-key controls with maxima 0.08-0.12 (computation still running); criterion >= 0.90 fixed in advance: failed at that threshold; 444 confirmed as the key of 1783-88.

credits.note: the King's cabinet: key ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska' of 8 Mar 1783, and the clear texts of 1786-87 in AKP 269 (not used for the readings)
key 444 transcribed and tested (failed at 0.90); ZbPop 3 sorted by system; 14 pieces transcribed and read in part blind (p13, p21, p28, p33, g1, g3 without a known clear), summaries in English
catalogue entries 415/416 and the deboli1788-1791 work and texts

gaps.detail: misread digits of the despatches, values of 444 that do not fit, and torn key entries 1215, 1216, 1398, 1405
a new test on three 1786 despatches with clears in AKP 269 is pre-registered, not yet run
no key of the time found; tables being learned on pairs with AKP 269

outcome.notes: A partial reading explained, published at Brice Dudout's request: no piece reaches 95%; for 8 of the 14 pieces a clear of the time probably exists in AKP 269 (kept unopened), so their content is probably existing and our reading is blind; the reading of the other six is new, in part. The key is of the time; the transcription is ours (CC BY 4.0).

prior.where: The cabinet's clear texts of 1786-87 are in AGAD AKP 1/11/0/-/269 (header index: a clear of the same date for 8 of the 14 pieces; none for p13, p21, p28, p33, g1, g3); not opened by the reading agent. No edition of 1786-87 (the IH PAN edition stops at 1782). Catalogue 416 open; no target on origin/main (GitHub API, 6 Nov 2026).

human: Brice Dudout obtained the scans, set the rules (protocols hashed before each step, threshold fixed in advance, clears of the time kept unopened) and answered blind shape plates on single digits (shapes only). AI agents transcribed the key and the despatches, tested the key, read and summarised. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the readings.
